Subject: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — networking & control plane questions

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the time earlier — great conversation and really appreciate the detail from your infra/security teams. As promised, a short recap and the next steps so we can get the networking/control-plane evaluation moving: 

Summary of what we heard from Acme:
- Requirement: Private deployment (VPC) with optional on-prem air-gapped mode for PHI-restricted workloads.
- Key concerns: control plane topology, egress minimization, cert/key management, and proof of isolation for audits.
- Success criteria for PoC: ability to spin up a private cluster in your VPC, run a set of inference tests that match your traffic pattern, and demonstrate no outbound egress other than customer-managed telemetry endpoints (if any).

What Redwood will provide next:
- Architecture reference (attached) showing both VPC-hosted control plane and customer-managed control plane variants.
- Networking checklist (attached) that maps required ports, subnets, and peering/bastion patterns.
- Proposed tests: 1) connectivity/throughput with our test harness, 2) KV/prefix cache persistence validation, 3) air-gap install dry-run for on-prem package.

High-level differentiators vs hyperscalers/other inference APIs (quick bullets):
- Control plane flexibility: we offer a customer-managed control plane option so you can keep the control plane inside your VPC (reduces compliance surface vs public control planes).
- Deterministic inference runtime: optimized kernels and predictable batching mean smaller tail latency variance for production workloads vs generic endpoints.
- Air-gapped installer: packaged on-prem bundle with documented install steps and KMS/HSM integration options.

Next steps / asks from Acme:
1) Can your infra/security team review the attached architecture and the networking checklist and call out any hard blockers?
2) Please confirm a point of contact for the PoC network changes (VPC peering, transit gateway, or direct connect).
3) If relevant, please share the preferred two-week window for the PoC. Our tentative slot is Dec 6-17.

Cc'd Camila (solutions engineer) and Marissa (product lead) who will run the tests and coordinate the air-gap evaluation.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / Marissa —

Putting together the test plan for Acme. A few internal notes and asks so we can answer Emily's Qs cleanly: 
- Customer-managed control plane: outbound telemetry is optional. We default to push logs/metrics to the customer's chosen telemetry collector (e.g., Datadog in their VPC) or to a bucket in the customer's account. We do not require a Redwood-managed endpoint, but some managed features (self-updates, metrics aggregation) rely on outbound connectivity if enabled.
- Air-gap installs: installer can be run fully offline if the customer provides container artifacts and licenses. For most customers we provide an archive with images and a signed license file; no external callouts are required at runtime.
- Runbooks: I have a short smoke-runbook draft — attaching the internal checklist and I'll export a customer-facing runbook.

Questions for product: Marissa, can you confirm the RBAC and KMS integration matrix we should surface to Acme? Also want to include a one-page competitive note vs HyperscalerX and OtherProvider that highlights control-plane and egress differences.

Emily —

Thanks for the follow-up. Quick answers inline below and a proposed next-steps timeline: 

1) Outbound control-plane telemetry: optional and customer-configurable.
- If Acme chooses the customer-managed control plane, the default is no outbound traffic to Redwood. You can opt into telemetry and auto-updates; those require outbound to configured endpoints, but we can use customer-hosted endpoints (e.g., a metrics bucket or private telemetry collector in your VPC).

2) Air-gapped installs: installer requirements
- Installer archive contains all container images and signed binaries. We require a one-time license activation token, but we can also support an offline activation flow where a signed activation file is exchanged manually if needed. No runtime internet access is required.

3) Runbooks/Test harness:
- Camila will share a customer-facing smoke-runbook (we've attached the internal checklist for transparency). For the PoC we suggest: 
  a) Internal smoke test (you run): run local smoke harness to validate networking + auth.
  b) Redwood-managed run: we run the inference workload inside your VPC with our test clients to validate latency/cost.
  c) Air-gap dry-run: perform staged installer run in a sandbox host to validate the operator steps.

Competitive notes (concise):
- HyperscalerX: offers managed endpoints but control plane remains outside customer VPC; difficult to demonstrate air-gapped installs and outbound-free operations.
- OtherProvider: cheaper list price but higher tail-latency and limited support for customer-managed control plane.
- Redwood: customer-managed control plane option + documented air-gap install + runtime optimizations for predictable latency.

Proposed timeline:
- Nov 29: security review of attached architecture
- Dec 6-10: internal smoke tests (Acme-run)
- Dec 13-17: Redwood-run inference tests + air-gap dry-run

If that works I'll have Camila coordinate the runbook handoff and Marissa prepare the RBAC/KMS doc you requested. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk the arch if useful.

Best,
Vanessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
